source: Polu & Sutskever (2020) Generative Language Modeling for Automated Theorem Proving (GPT-f)
finding: A transformer prover with best-first search beat the prior Metamath state of the art. Bigger models did better. Text pre-training helped.
numbers: Metamath held-out test: 56.22% vs 21.16% for MetaGen-IL. Model size 160m/400m/700m: 28.96/30.23/31.58% (same 18B tokens). 160m CommonCrawl pre-trained: 32.34% vs 28.96% from scratch.
limits: Metamath is low level. Some comparisons are within typical variance. About 1k GPU hours per 700m evaluation.
agent_relevance: A learned model proposes, a formal checker disposes. Maps to generate-then-verify (S8).

source: Lample et al. (2022) HyperTree Proof Search (Evariste)
finding: Online training on unproved statements raised pass rates. HTPS beat GPT-f on Lean and Metamath.
numbers: Metamath held-out: 82.6% after online training. miniF2F-valid pass@64: 58.6% (GPT-f 47.3). miniF2F-curriculum 31% to 42%. Top setting cost 1360 A100 days.
limits: Numbers marked cumulative are on statements seen during online training, so not a clean test. Very high compute.
agent_relevance: Verified outputs are the training signal; our scaffold cannot train, but can reuse verified results.

source: Jiang et al. (2022) Draft, Sketch, and Prove
finding: Informal proof drafts turned into formal sketches, with Sledgehammer closing the gaps, beat direct proving. Each part of the pipeline carries weight.
numbers: miniF2F-test: Sledgehammer 20.9%, Sledgehammer+heuristics 35.2% (valid 18.0%), Thor 29.9%, DSP with human informal proof 38.9% (valid 42.6%). Ablations on valid: no in-line comments -4.9; no informal proof -3.7; no automated prover -9.8. On test, bigger Minerva drafter was worse: 8B 36.5%, 62B 34.0%, 540B 30.3%.
limits: Used original miniF2F statements, which have known errors. Test and valid disagree on which drafter is best.
agent_relevance: Closest match to our design: plan in words, formalize skeleton, let a mechanical tool close the leaves. The automated prover is the biggest single part.

source: Jiang et al. (2022) Thor: Wielding Hammers to Integrate Language Models and Automated Theorem Provers
finding: Letting the language model call Sledgehammer at chosen steps lifted success on PISA and solved problems neither could alone.
numbers: PISA: 39.0% to 57.0%. 8.2% of problems solved that neither LM nor Sledgehammer solved alone. miniF2F 1-pass 29.6% to 29.9% with much less compute. LM steps with premise selection advanced the proof 1.9% of the time vs 28.2% for steps without premises.
limits: Isabelle only.
agent_relevance: Delegate premise search and gap closing to a classical prover; keep the model for strategy.

source: Mikula et al. (2023/2024) Magnushammer: A Transformer-Based Approach to Premise Selection
finding: Contrastive retrieval of premises beat Sledgehammer's hand-built selection. With an LM prover it set a new Isabelle record.
numbers: PISA: 59.5% vs 38.3% Sledgehammer. miniF2F: 34.0% vs 20.9%. With LM prover PISA 57.0% to 71.0% using 4x fewer parameters.
limits: Isabelle; needs a large premise dataset for training.
agent_relevance: Finding the right lemma is a bottleneck. A lemma library with good retrieval is worth building.

source: Yang et al. (2023) LeanDojo: Theorem Proving with Retrieval-Augmented Language Models
finding: Premise retrieval helps, more on theorems needing new premises. GPT-4 zero-shot was weak. A benchmark checker was found to misjudge correct proofs.
numbers: Pass@1 random split: ReProver 51.2%, without retrieval 47.6%, GPT-4 29.0%, tidy 23.8%. novel_premises split: 26.3 / 23.2 / 7.4 / 5.3. miniF2F 26.5%, ProofNet 13.8%. A prior benchmark misjudged 21.1% of correct proofs as wrong; fixed to 1.4%.
limits: Random split inflates scores; novel_premises about halves them. Small ByT5 model.
agent_relevance: Test on held-out premises, not random splits. A buggy checker gives false failures, so check the checker.

source: First et al. (2023) Baldur: Whole-Proof Generation and Repair with Large Language Models
finding: Whole-proof generation beat step-wise search. Feeding the checker's error message back to repair gave a small, real gain.
numbers: 6,336 Isabelle theorems: whole proofs 47.9% vs 39.0% for search. Repair with error message +1.5% even at equal compute. With Thor: 65.7% total; Baldur proves an extra 8.7% over Thor.
limits: Error message was crucial for repair. Gain is modest.
agent_relevance: Supports a verify-and-repair loop using the real checker message, with small expected gain per round.

source: Tsoukalas et al. (2024) PutnamBench
finding: A hard undergraduate competition benchmark in Lean 4, Isabelle and Coq. Early systems solved almost nothing.
numbers: 640 Lean/Isabelle and 412 Coq problems. Lean: GPT-4 1/640, COPRA 1/640, ReProver 0/640. Isabelle: DSP 4/640, Sledgehammer 3/640. Coq: GPT-4 1, COPRA 1, CoqHammer 0, Tactician 0 of 412.
limits: Early 2024 snapshot. Later systems moved far (see b15, b18).
agent_relevance: Shows the cliff between high-school and undergraduate level. Keep a fresh held-out set.

source: Xin et al. (2024) DeepSeek-Prover-V1.5
finding: RL from proof-assistant feedback plus tree search lifted pass rates. Chain-of-thought helped. RL gain did not fade at larger budgets.
numbers: miniF2F-test single-pass whole-proof 60.2% (V1: 50.0%); with RMaxTS tree search 63.5%. ProofNet test 25.3% with search. Pass@128 with CoT: 51.6% miniF2F, 18.2% ProofNet; CoT beat non-CoT in most settings.
limits: Whole-proof and search budgets are not compute-matched.
agent_relevance: Reasoning before each step helps even for formal output. Truncate at first error then resume is a reusable repair pattern.

source: Pan et al. (2023) Logic-LM: Empowering Large Language Models with Symbolic Solvers
finding: LLM translates to logic, a solver reasons, a refinement step fixes parse errors. Beat standard and CoT prompting on logic benchmarks.
numbers: Average gain over standard prompting 39.2% and over CoT 18.4% (GPT-3.5); GPT-4 gains 24.98% and 10.44%. Executable rate: FOLIO 66.7% (GPT-3.5) and 79.9% (GPT-4), raised to 84.3% and 85.8% with self-refinement. ProntoQA 99.4-100%.
limits: GPT-4 gain on FOLIO is small. Falls back to CoT when parse fails.
agent_relevance: Use a solver for exact deduction; plan for translation failure with a fallback.

source: Olausson et al. (2023) LINC: Logical Inference via Neurosymbolic Computation
finding: Offloading deduction to Prover9 helped small models a lot and big models only on some data. Translation loss is the main failure.
numbers: FOLIO StarCoder+: 56.0% LINC vs 41.8% closest control. ProofWriter GPT-3.5 96.4%, GPT-4 98.3% with LINC. FOLIO GPT-4: LINC 72.5% vs CoT 75.3% average. LINC predicts Uncertain 57% vs CoT 41%. FOL syntax errors: 38% StarCoder+, 24% GPT-3.5, 13% GPT-4.
limits: GPT-4 on FOLIO: no benefit. Translating text to FOL is lossy, so a sound prover still rests on a lossy translation.
agent_relevance: Verified deduction pays off for deep chains; for naturalistic text, record what the formalization dropped.

source: Ren et al. (2025) DeepSeek-Prover-V2
finding: A general model decomposes into subgoals, a small prover solves them; this gives cold-start data for RL. CoT mode far outperformed non-CoT.
numbers: miniF2F-test 88.9% at pass@8192 (671B CoT), 82.0% at pass@1024. 7B CoT 77.87% at pass@1024 vs 7B non-CoT 52.94% at pass@1 (different budgets); non-CoT 671B 80.74%. PutnamBench 47/658. ProverBench AIME: 6 of 15 vs DeepSeek-V3 majority vote 8 of 15. Mean output tokens on miniF2F: CoT 6751.9 vs non-CoT 761.8 (671B).
limits: CoT costs about 9x the tokens. Top results use thousands of samples.
agent_relevance: Subgoal decomposition is the proven mechanism for the subgoal library. Reasoning costs tokens.

source: Wang et al. (2025) Kimina-Prover Preview
finding: RL-trained reasoning-style prover is sample efficient and scales with model size, a trend not seen before for provers.
numbers: miniF2F-test 80.7% at pass@8192; strong at pass@1; scaling with size across 1.5B, 7B, 72B distilled/base.
limits: Preview release; claims later overtaken.
agent_relevance: Long reasoning before the formal step gives sample efficiency.

source: Lin et al. (2025) Goedel-Prover-V2
finding: Small provers with verifier-guided self-correction beat much larger ones. Compiler feedback adds a couple of points.
numbers: 8B: 84.6% pass@32 on miniF2F, above DeepSeek-Prover-V2-671B (80x larger). 32B: 88.1% pass@32, 90.4% with self-correction. PutnamBench 44 solved, 57 with self-correction at pass@32; 86 at pass@184 (prior open record 47 at pass@1024).
limits: Self-correction is serial and costs tokens. Model averaging needed to keep output diversity.
agent_relevance: Verifier-guided revision gives a measurable but small gain; scaffolded easier-first synthetic tasks help.

source: ByteDance Seed (2025) Seed-Prover: Deep and Broad Reasoning for Automated Theorem Proving
finding: Lemma-style whole-proof model using Lean feedback, proved lemmas and self-summary. Largest jump on hard benchmarks.
numbers: Past IMO problems 78.1%. miniF2F-test 99.6% (valid 100%). PutnamBench 331/657 (prior best 86/657). IMO 2025: 4/6 in competition, 5/6 after. Seed-Geometry solves 43 of IMO-AG-50 vs AlphaGeometry 2's 42.
limits: Proprietary; heavy test-time compute. miniF2F no longer discriminates.
agent_relevance: Reusing proved lemmas across attempts is the library idea at work.

source: Chervonyi et al. (2025) Gold-medalist Performance in Solving Olympiad Geometry with AlphaGeometry2
finding: Neuro-symbolic geometry: a symbolic deduction engine plus language-model proposals of constructions.
numbers: Language coverage of IMO 2000-2024 geometry from 66% to 88%. Solve rate 84% over 25 years vs 54% before. Part of the IMO 2024 silver-medal system.
limits: Closed domain with its own symbolic engine.
agent_relevance: The sound engine does deduction; the model only proposes auxiliary constructions.

source: Song, Yang, Anandkumar (2024) Towards Large Language Models as Copilots for Theorem Proving in Lean
finding: On the Mathematics in Lean textbook, LLM proof search automated more steps than rule-based Aesop.
numbers: Proof steps automated: 74.2% (search proof) vs 58.4% (suggest tactics) vs 40.1% (Aesop). Aesop proved 24.4% of theorems autonomously, needing 3.86 human tactics on average.
limits: Textbook-level theorems only.
agent_relevance: Mixed rule-based plus LLM beats either alone; automate easy steps, hand the rest to the model.

source: Hilbert team (2025) Hilbert: Recursively Building Formal Proofs with Informal Reasoning
finding: An agent combining a general reasoning model, a specialist prover, a Lean verifier and retrieval, with recursive decomposition, beat each part alone.
numbers: miniF2F 99.2% with Gemini 2.5 Pro + Goedel-32B (+24.6 over Goedel pass@4 baseline). Gemini 2.5 Pro alone pass@16384: 49.1%. PutnamBench 462/660 (70.0%) vs Seed-Prover 50.4%; with gpt-oss-120b as reasoner only 88/660 (13.3%). Retrieval ablation: 99.2% vs 97.9% (Goedel), 98.4% vs 97.1% (DeepSeek); reasoner tokens 4.0M to 2.3M.
limits: Result depends strongly on the informal reasoner (13.3% vs 70.0%). Millions of tokens per problem.
agent_relevance: Closest published design to our scaffold. Reasoner quality matters more than prover. Retrieval cuts cost.

source: Robinson (1965) A Machine-Oriented Logic Based on the Resolution Principle
finding: Introduced resolution with unification as a complete inference rule for first-order logic. Basis of saturation provers such as Vampire and E.
numbers: No experiment; completeness theorem. Not opened this session.
limits: Pure resolution explodes combinatorially, hence later orderings, selection and indexing. Background only.
agent_relevance: Complete is not tractable; search control is needed.

source: Sutcliffe, CADE ATP System Competition (CASC-J12 results page)
finding: Annual first-order prover competition. The fetched page was too large to read; Vampire versions led the THF listing I could see.
numbers: No counts extracted.
limits: Problems come from TPTP, which provers are tuned on.
agent_relevance: Do not cite counts from this line.

source: Synthesis: miniF2F and PutnamBench saturation
finding: miniF2F-test rose from 29.9% (Thor, 2022) to 99.6% (Seed-Prover, 2025). PutnamBench rose from 1/640 (2024) to 331/657 and 462/660 in 2025.
numbers: miniF2F-test: Thor 29.9, DeepSeek-V1.5 63.5, DeepSeek-V2 88.9, Seed-Prover 99.6. PutnamBench: GPT-4 1, DeepSeek-V2 47, Goedel-V2 86, Seed 331, Hilbert 462.
limits: Different compute budgets; proprietary systems not reproducible; contamination not ruled out in these papers.
agent_relevance: Treat any single benchmark number as perishable.

source: Synthesis: which pipeline parts carry the gain
finding: Across DSP, Baldur, Goedel-V2 and Hilbert the parts that mattered were: a mechanical prover for leaves, real checker error text for repair, decomposition, and retrieval.
numbers: DSP no prover -9.8 points; Baldur repair +1.5; Goedel self-correction about +2; Hilbert retrieval +1.3 points and about 43% fewer reasoner tokens (4.0M to 2.3M); Hilbert full 99.2% vs reasoner alone 49.1%.
limits: Measured by different groups on different data; effects not additive.
agent_relevance: Order of investment for verify stage: mechanical leaf-closer, decomposition, retrieval, then repair loop.

source: Synthesis: failure modes and boundary conditions
finding: Scores fall on held-out premises, undergraduate level, naturalistic text translation, and with a weak informal reasoner.
numbers: LeanDojo novel_premises 26.3 vs random 51.2. Early PutnamBench 0-4 of 640. LINC GPT-4 FOLIO 72.5% vs CoT 75.3%. Hilbert with weak reasoner 13.3% vs 70.0%.
limits: Secondary synthesis of b06, b08, b11, b18.
agent_relevance: Formalizing is the weak link; verify the translation as well as the proof.

source: Synthesis: compute cost of reasoning provers
finding: Reasoning mode gives higher pass rates at about 9x the tokens. Top scores use thousands of samples. Small RL-trained models can match much larger ones at lower budget.
numbers: DeepSeek-V2 CoT 6751.9 vs 761.8 tokens. 88.9% needs pass@8192. Goedel-8B 84.6% at pass@32 beats 671B DeepSeek-V2 at the same metric. Hilbert 2.3M-4.0M reasoner tokens per problem.
limits: Cross-paper comparison.
agent_relevance: Our scaffold needs explicit token budgets and an early stop once the checker passes.

source: Synthesis: whole-proof versus step-wise search
finding: Whole-proof generation with repair overtook step-wise search from 2023. Search still adds a little on top.
numbers: Baldur 47.9% vs 39.0% search. DeepSeek-V1.5 whole-proof 60.2% vs 63.5% with MCTS.
limits: Different datasets across papers.
agent_relevance: Generate a whole plan, check, repair; use search only as a booster.
